extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: A benchmark of 1,825 executable queries across nine domains for evaluating LLM-generated interactive visual artifacts. Tasks have task-specific, ten-dimension checklists and Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty tiers, with 559/611/655 tasks respectively. The automated evaluation assesses code quality, visual fidelity, and interactive behavior using source code and three staged execution screenshots.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.citeAs: Tencent Hunyuan Team. ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation. arXiv:2507.04952v2, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Candidates are aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM-generated queries derived from screenshots. Automated filtering produces a curated pool that seeds further expansion. The construction pipeline combines expert sourcing, LLM generation and rewriting, human verification, de-duplication, checklist calibration, and solvability validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Incomplete candidates are dropped by automated filters, and underspecified tasks are pruned during solvability validation. Query quality filtering explicitly checks that descriptions contain no critical missing information and provide sufficient conditions for a correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and screenshots used for LLM visual-to-query generation.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Experts rewrite prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting introduces diverse styles, followed by human verification. Items flagged as duplicates are re-authored or discarded. Tasks solvable only through brittle hacks are revised or removed. Difficulty tiers are assigned post hoc using aggregated performance of more than 30 models, producing 559 Easy, 611 Medium, and 655 Hard tasks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters remove incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive candidates. Two-stage de-duplication uses MinHash and semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, followed by screenshot perceptual hashing to detect visually near-identical artifacts. Candidate solutions from multiple model families support solvability checks and removal of underspecified tasks. Execution is standardized using Playwright with headless Chromium at 1024×768 resolution and deterministic seeds, capturing screenshots before, during, and after scripted interaction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query receives a ten-dimension checklist drafted by Hunyuan-Turbos and refined by humans for specificity and screenability. Five dimensions are vision-oriented and five are code-oriented, with each dimension scored on a ten-point scale. A 10% manually curated seed supplies few-shot calibration references. Gemini-2.5-Pro classifies queries by category and visual interactivity; subcategory tags receive human spot-checks. Difficulty labels are derived from aggregated model performance. For human validation, 280 randomly selected queries with responses from six models are independently scored by multiple experienced front-end engineers under a double-blind protocol, with randomized sample order.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The manually curated checklist seed achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators. Human ground-truth scores are the median of individual annotator ratings. Automated-versus-human agreement is measured using Pair ACC, the proportion of response pairs with concordant rankings, reaching 90.95% for Gemini-2.5-Pro with multiple screenshots. Dual-referee rankings show highly consistent partial-order constraints, with residual differences concentrated among top systems. Replacing Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro preserves identical partial-order constraints. Difficulty stratification is stable under leave-family-out resampling.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Human validation annotators are engineers with extensive front-end development experience.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos for checklist generation; Gemini-2.5-Pro for query classification and automated scoring; Qwen2.5-VL-72B for automated scoring; Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 for reported baseline scoring.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Query quality filtering aims to select privacy-free queries. Its privacy criterion checks whether a query avoids requesting or involving sensitive personal information, including phone numbers, addresses, and other identifiable details.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide a scalable, accurate evaluation tool that accelerates development of user-centric generative models. The paper emphasizes that visual fidelity and functional interaction directly affect user experience and real-world adoption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential cognitive biases in how different multimodal referees interpret long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback. Code-aware referee judgments can diverge from human preferences because they account for engineering qualities that human voting may underweight. Human validation uses double-blinding and randomized sample order to mitigate bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Three screenshots sampled at fixed intervals may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions, including multi-step web workflows and nuanced game physics. The benchmark evaluates the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative refinement, autonomous debugging, or multi-step agentic development. Multimodal judges can exhibit hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited engineering/code-quality awareness, and version drift; the framework introduces structured safeguards but still shows discrepancies with human judgments.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and benchmarking LLMs on single-turn generation of executable visual artifacts from multimodal instructions. Supports comparisons across domains, difficulty tiers, and interactivity levels, with fine-grained diagnostics of visual quality, interaction correctness, and code quality. The released benchmark, dataset specifications, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, referee settings, evaluation harness, and baseline results support reproducible evaluation.
